name: TPS26601RHFR
title: TPS2660x: 60 V, 2 A industrial eFuse with built-in reverse input polarity protection
summary: An eFuse for 4.2 V to 60 V DC rails with two back-to-back N-channel FETs inside (150 mΩ total) that survives and blocks input voltages down to -60 V without an external diode. One resistor sets the current limit from 0.1 A to 2.23 A; resistors set undervoltage and overvoltage trip points, a capacitor sets the output ramp, and the MODE pin picks active current limiting or an electronic circuit breaker, each latching or retrying. It blocks reverse current, reports faults on an open-drain FLT pin and gives a current proportional to load current on IMON. TPS26600 and TPS26602 retry after a breaker trip with MODE open, TPS26601 latches; TPS26602 clamps the output at a fixed 38 V instead of cutting off. TPS26601RHFR is the latching part in the 24-pin VQFN on a 3000-piece reel.
key_figures: 4.2 V to 60 V (62 V absolute maximum)
0.1 A to 2.23 A, set by R(ILIM) of 120 kΩ to 5.36 kΩ

circuits.title: Simplified schematic
circuits.description: The basic connection: a three-resistor divider from the input sets the UVLO and OVP trip points, a capacitor on dVdT sets the turn-on ramp, R(ILIM) sets the current limit and R(IMON) turns the IMON current into a voltage for a load monitor. MODE is tied to RTN for current limiting with auto-retry. FLT is pulled up to the output and read as a health signal; SHDN takes an on/off control. All the setting parts return to RTN; GND goes to system ground.

circuits.title: 24 V, 1 A eFuse input protection for an industrial PLC CPU
circuits.description: A 24 V input protector worked out in full: R1, R2 and R3 put the undervoltage trip at 18 V and the overvoltage cut-off at 30 V, 11.8 kΩ on ILIM sets a 1 A limit, 33.2 kΩ on IMON gives about 2.5 V at the limit for a 0-2.5 V ADC, and 2.2 µF on dVdT stretches the ramp into the 2.2 mF load to about 0.53 s so inrush stays near 0.1 A. MODE to RTN gives current limiting with auto-retry. FLT is pulled up to the output by 100 kΩ.
notes: Design targets: V(UV) 18 V, V(OV) 30 V, current limit 1 A, C(OUT) 2200 µF, start-up load 48 Ω, TA up to 85 °C.

circuits.title: Active ORing of two supplies
circuits.description: Two eFuses, each with its own UVLO/OVP divider, dVdT capacitor and current-limit resistor, have their outputs joined to feed one load from either of two supplies. Each part's reverse comparator turns its FETs off when its output stands above its input, so the higher supply carries the load and no current flows back into the lower one, without the drop of an ORing diode. MODE is tied to RTN on both.

circuits.title: Simple 24 V supply path protection
circuits.description: The fewest parts: only R(ILIM), CIN and COUT. UVLO, OVP and MODE are tied to RTN, which selects the internal 15 V undervoltage and 33 V overvoltage thresholds and current limiting with auto-retry; dVdT is left open for the internal ramp of about 24 V in 1.6 ms. FLT, SHDN and IMON are not used.

parts.value: Input from a 24 V power supply

circuits.title: Circuit with optional transient protection parts
circuits.description: The full connection with the parts added for surge and switching transients: a bidirectional TVS from the input to ground clamps input spikes, and a Schottky diode from ground to the output catches the negative spike an inductive output produces when the FETs interrupt current. R4 pulls FLT up to the output; R(IMON) loads IMON. MODE is tied to RTN. SHDN is not connected.

operation.text: TPS26600 and TPS26601 cut the output off on overvoltage at an adjustable level; TPS26602 instead holds the output at a fixed 38 V. With MODE open, TPS26600 and TPS26602 behave as a circuit breaker that retries, TPS26601 as one that latches. All three offer current limiting with retry (MODE to RTN) or latch (402 kΩ to RTN).

When UVLO falls below V(UVLOF) the FETs turn off quickly and FLT goes low; the comparator has 90 mV of hysteresis. A divider from IN to UVLO to RTN sets the level. With UVLO tied to RTN an internal 15 V threshold with 1 V hysteresis is used; with UVLO tied to IN the function is off. UVLO must not float.
Below the POR threshold on IN the internal circuits are disabled. The POR threshold has 275 mV of hysteresis; V(PORF) is 3.72 V, and falling below it also clears FLT.

On TPS26600 and TPS26601 a voltage above V(OVPR) on OVP turns the FET off. A divider from IN to OVP to RTN sets the level, or OVP tied to RTN selects an internal 33 V threshold with 2 V hysteresis. The largest external setting is 55 V. TPS26602 has OVP tied to RTN and clamps the output at V(OVC) when the input exceeds 38 V; the FET then dissipates (VIN - VOVC) × IOUT, and a long clamp can end in thermal shutdown.

The reverse protection is built in, so no series diode is needed, and the part survives -60 V on its input. The protection sits between RTN and GND inside the device: tying RTN to GND removes it, and a reversed input then destroys the part.

A fast comparator watches V(IN) - V(OUT). The FETs turn off within 1.5 µs typ once it falls below -110 mV and turn back on within 40 µs typ once it exceeds 100 mV, which lets two parts share a load as an ideal-diode OR. An unpowered part in such a pair shows about 0.7 V on its control pins against GND, so its IMON and FLT readings are to be ignored.

A capacitor from dVdT to RTN sets the output slew rate at turn-on, limiting the dip on a live backplane. Left open, the internal ramp is 23.9 V per 1.6 ms; a capacitor only makes it slower. A 5 µA source charges dVdT and the output follows at 24.6 times its voltage; a 14 Ω switch discharges it when the part is off.

With MODE to RTN or 402 kΩ to RTN the part holds the load current at I(OL), set by R(ILIM). FLT goes low after 875 µs. The output sags and dissipation rises; at T(TSD) the FET turns off. In latch-off mode it stays off until V(IN) drops below V(PORF) or SHDN is toggled; in auto-retry mode it restarts 512 ms after TJ falls below T(TSD) - 10 °C. FLT stays low until the fault clears.

With MODE open, overload current is allowed to flow while it stays below I(FASTRIP). A timer starts when the load exceeds I(CB); after tCB(dly) the FET turns off and FLT goes low. The latching version stays off until V(IN) drops below V(PORF) or SHDN is toggled; the retrying version tries again after 540 ms.

The current-limit loop is too slow for a hard short, so a fast-trip comparator at I(FASTRIP) = 1.87 × I(OL) + 0.015 turns the FET off within 250 ns typ. It holds it off for a few microseconds, then turns it back on slowly and the limit loop takes over at I(OL), after which the part behaves as in an overload. Started into a shorted output it limits to I(OL) from the beginning.

FLT is open-drain and active low. It goes low on undervoltage, overvoltage, overload, reverse current and thermal shutdown, in shutdown with SHDN low, and during start-up until the FET gate is fully enhanced: an internal power-good signal is ORed into it, so it can serve as a power-good input for downstream converters. Faults are deglitched inside. FLT may be left open or tied to RTN when unused. With a reversed input, the interface from FLT to downstream logic needs care.
In current-limit operation, an overload lasting longer than tPGOODF (875 µs typ) pulls FLT low as a warning that thermal shutdown is coming; FLT stays low until the fault is gone.

IMON sources a current proportional to the IN to OUT current; a resistor to RTN turns it into a voltage. The output is linear up to the lower of V(IN) - 1.5 V and 4 V. No capacitor goes on IMON, since it would delay the reading. With a reversed input, 100 kΩ in series between IMON and an ADC limits current into the ADC's ESD structures.
Above T(TSD) the FETs turn off and FLT goes low. Depending on the mode the part latches off or retries 512 ms after TJ falls below T(TSD) - 10 °C.

Pulling SHDN below 0.76 V turns the FETs off and cuts quiescent current to 20 µA typ. SHDN has an internal pull-up; holding it low takes a pull-down able to sink 10 µA or more while at 400 mV, and the pin must rise to at least 1 V to enable. It can be driven by a microcontroller GPIO or by the transistor of an opto-isolator (collector to SHDN, emitter to GND). On enable the FETs turn on through the dVdT ramp.

RFLTb, the FLT pull-up, is typically 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ; FLT sinks no more than 10 mA. CIN, the local input bypass, is typically 0.1 µF to 1 µF. Start-up dissipation, with and without load, must stay inside the thermal shutdown time at the chosen ramp, with at least 30 % margin; a larger C(dVdT) lowers it. In the example, 2.2 µF and a 528 ms ramp are within limits for a 48 Ω load.

The supply range is 4.2 V to 60 V. With the source more than a few inches away, a ceramic input capacitor above 0.1 µF is used. The source must be able to supply more than the set current limit. Interrupting current makes input inductance kick positive and output inductance kick negative, which can exceed the absolute maximum ratings: short leads, a large ground plane, a Schottky diode across the output and a small ceramic input capacitor (about 0.1 µF) help. Where surge tests call for a TVS, at least 1 µF on the input keeps the input falling slew rate within 20 V/µs.

In I/O modules fed from a field supply the part guards the field loads against under-, over- and reverse voltage, limits the module's share of a supply common to many modules, isolates a shorted load fast enough that the other modules keep running, and blocks reverse current when the output side is miswired. IMON and FLT give load monitoring and diagnostics through a digital isolator.

Place 0.1 µF or more of ceramic capacitance between IN and GND, closest to those pins, with a small loop. Power paths are short and sized for at least twice the full-load current. RTN is a copper plane or island. R(ILIM), C(dVdT), R(IMON) and the MODE, UVLO and OVP resistors sit close to their pins and return to RTN by the shortest trace; the ILIM and IMON traces are kept short and away from switching signals. TVS, snubbers and protection diodes sit close to what they protect, the output Schottky close to OUT and GND. The PowerPAD is soldered to the RTN plane under the part; other layers can add heat sinking. Designs without reverse polarity protection may join RTN, GND and PowerPAD to the ground plane.

UL 2367 recognized, file 169910, for RILIM ≥ 5.36 kΩ (2.35 A maximum). Safe under UL60950 single point failure testing, with open and short ILIM detection. Documentation for functional safety system design is offered.
